gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-numans: Numans spreads its letters out with generous tracking and rope-like fullness. Conthrax counters with a single plotter-pen line that stays crisp and engineered, while the plain sans body is the one built to be lived in.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-onest: Conthrax is all geometric precision, drawn with a wide-mouthed a and capitals that barely clear the lowercase. Onest comes in friendlier, with short ascenders over big bowls and a smooth, gentle line that softens the whole look.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-open-sans: Machined and sleek, Conthrax looks like bent tubing, with the same gauge running through every letter. Open Sans settles in beside it with bulky lowercase proportions and smooth curves that never clog, giving the page a warmer, easier footing.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-oxygen: Conthrax draws its strokes like a bent paperclip, geometric and wide-mouthed, with lowercase that nearly merges into its capitals. And Oxygen answers that rigidity with curves that never close back on themselves, loosening the feel without losing the tidy look.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-preahvihear: Sharp, techy and drawn with one tip. Preahvihear follows with a mouth as open as a pried oyster shell and a lofty x-height, so paragraphs would feel spacious and unhurried beneath Conthrax.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption brings big-bodied lowercase and bowls that feel unclosed and inviting. And under Conthrax, whose strokes show essentially no contrast, paragraphs would read with a welcoming, steady flow rather than a stiff one.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-puritan: Approachable and clean, Puritan keeps its rounded forms open to the side, with oversized e and a counters. Conthrax adds no thin strokes to vanish in glare.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-questrial: Modern and tidy, Questrial cuts open c, e and s shapes from single-weight strokes with short stalks above. Paragraphs would glide along beneath Conthrax without a snag.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-radio-canada: Conthrax stretches wide and geometric, with a wide-mouthed a and a single-thread rhythm in its lines. Radio Canada keeps its c, s and z full and its curves open at the ends, so long text moves smoothly.
gen-dafont-conthrax-gf-saira: Wide, sleek and machine-cut, Conthrax leads with a wide-mouthed a and a single-thread feel. And Saira follows with see-through s shapes and rounded letters stretching toward the top line, so extended text stays light and easy to follow.
